notes: Structured dossier layer. Existing values are archive-derived; empty arrays are deliberate expansion slots for future project-specific material.

ewp-project.title: EWP Project
ewp-project.summary: CGI abstract animation about a demon in human form returning to his hometown. The 2023 short combines abstract imagery with themes of alienation, identity and generational disconnect, with Ilya Minin (Eli) as director and a documented production crew.
process: CGI abstract animation built around a 3D production archive with character models, scenes and rigging assets.
Directed and scripted by Ilya Minin with a distributed crew across art production, animation, VFX, lighting, sound and narration.
The 2023 film was later prepared as a public Festival Cut in 2026.

chronology.note: Original CGI short produced.
Festival Cut published into the public archive.

archival_notes: The project archive preserves both production assets and the finished film, making the repository part of the work's history.
source_context: A mysterious traveler returns to his transformed hometown, where familiar places have become surreal landscapes and fragmented memories. Moving between decaying urban spaces, dreamlike plains, encounters with locals and another outsider, he is forced to confront his own divided identity and the uncertain boundary between memory, perception and truth.

Rather than presenting a conventional linear narrative, EWP Project uses metaphorical storytelling, surreal environments and subconscious imagery to explore belonging, memory, personal transformation and the search for self.

bogorodskoe.title: Bogorodskoe
bogorodskoe.summary: Experimental short film and comedy series about Bogorodskoye, created with Yulia Baranyuk in 2022. The project reconstructs local history through performance, theatre, music, dancing, fairground culture and deliberately chaotic contemporary video language, drawing on collected local-history essays and articles.
process: Contemporary film / comedy series built from local-history research about Bogorodskoye.
Combines historical reconstruction with performance, theater, music, dancing, fairground traditions and intentionally chaotic video language.
The project was made by Yulia Baranyuk and Ilya Minin with a wider documented cast and crew.

chronology.note: Experimental film and comedy project based on collected Bogorodskoye local-history material.

archival_notes: The source names Yulia Baranyuk, Anna Malakhova, Olga Romanova, Mel, Vasily Ivanov, Vladimir Pilikhovski, Sergey Bratkov and Oleg Ustinov in the cast.
source_context: Bogorodskoye (2022) is an experimental short film and comedy video series by Ilya Minin (Eli) and Yulia Baranyuk, inspired by the local history, theater, music, dancing, and fairground traditions of Bogorodskoye.

Set against the cultural world of late-19th-century Bogorodskoye, the project explores a place remembered through carnival, absurdity, performance, and chaotic everyday life. The series is based on local-history essays and articles collected in Bogorodskoye. Pages of History: A Collection of Local-History Essays and Articles by T. Z. Biryukova and A. V. Bugrov.

the-last-day-of-kasane-teto.title: The Last Day of Kasane Teto
source_context: The Last Day of Kasane Teto is an experimental animated short by Ilya Minin (Eli) exploring the fragile boundary between light and darkness.
Through Kasane Teto's final journey, the film turns an iconic virtual character into a vessel for questions about connection, isolation, inner demons, suffering and transformation.

triple-baka.title: Triple Baka
source_context: I made this animation because sometimes reality falters. A fog-stranded stroll, three strangers and an abandoned barn… those things aren’t “just an excuse.”

This cartoon is less about Teto, Miku, or Neru and more about how my brain translates cracks in existence. A 2008 track trickles through it all — Triple Baka — but here, the rhythm's warped and three idiots (me, them, whatever) caught in a loop labeled Tuesday.

eugene.title: 友人 / Eugene
eugene.summary: Japanese CVVC UTAU / OpenUtau voicebank by Ilya Minin (Eli), designed around a warm, intimate tone with a slightly uncanny edge. The released bank uses three recorded pitches and is documented for expressive Japanese singing, especially dark pop, industrial and experimental material.
process: Japanese CVVC voicebank built from preserved recordings, reconstructed phonemes and post-production.
Designed for UTAU / OpenUtau singing with a warm, intimate tone and a slightly uncanny edge.
Official documentation keeps technical specifications, usage, character and media history together.

chronology.note: Current released 友人 (Eugene) voicebank record in the public archive.

technical_notes: Recommended engine setup: TIPS; Moresampler, WORLDLINE-R and wavtool4vcv are also documented.
Genres documented: dark pop / industrial / experimental.
archival_notes: The character documentation frames Eugene through unfinished things, memory and disappearance; this is retained as a project/character description rather than a claim about the real voice provider.

iirai.title: イーライ / Iirai family
iirai.summary: Three-generation Japanese UTAU voicebank family: イーライ, 茜音イーライ and 茜音イーライ・暁. The project preserves earlier generations while developing new recordings, appends, technical documentation and character presentation.
process: Voicebank family developed through successive generations rather than replacing earlier versions.
Generation 1 preserves the original イーライ; Generation 2 established 茜音イーライ; Generation 3 暁 is an ongoing revision with cleaned samples, appends and extras.
Character, technical and release documentation are maintained together.

chronology.note: Original イーライ (Iirai).
茜音イーライ (Akane Iirai) released as the established updated CVVC bank.
茜音イーライ・暁 currently in development.

technical_notes: Generation 2 documents A3 / F3 / C3 pitches.
Recommended tools include TIPS, Moresampler, WORLDLINE-R and wavtool4vcv.

jihanki.title: JIHANKI
jihanki.summary: Web-based interactive archive presented as a Japanese vending machine interface, combining texts, sounds, photographs, scripts and project documentation. It grew from the SAIKONEON / Lake Saiko field experience in Japan and treats the vending machine as the archive's interaction model.
process: The project began from the SAIKONEON / Lake Saiko field experience in Japan and a nighttime encounter with a vending machine.
The vending-machine interface became a model for the archive itself: interaction returns fragments of memory rather than products.
Documents, photographs, sounds, scripts and field material are loaded into a lightweight static web application.

chronology.note: SAIKONEON / Lake Saiko residency and Japan field experience.
JIHANKI develops as an interactive archive around the field material.

technical_notes: Static web application; no backend or build step.
Fixed internal machine coordinate system with responsive scaling.
Archive material is separated into notes, projects, scripts and yokai documentation.
archival_notes: The project explicitly treats interface, collection and classification as part of the artwork rather than an after-the-fact presentation layer.

mountain-remembers.title: 山は覚えている / The Mountain Remembers
mountain-remembers.summary: Experimental audiovisual work built from a Fuji-area journey, field recordings, memory and folklore; uses Akane Iirai, Eugene and Takismana.
process: Constructed from an actual Fuji-area journey, field recordings and fragments of memory rather than as a conventional travel documentary.
Roads, forests, shrines, tunnels, lakes, vending machines, voices and mechanical sounds are reorganized into an imagined audiovisual landscape.
UTAU voicebanks are integrated as remembered or returning voices within the landscape.

chronology.note: Fuji Five Lakes / Aokigahara / Lake Saiko field journey and audiovisual reconstruction.

archival_notes: The source description explicitly distinguishes the work from documentary representation of Japan; it is indexed as a transformation of journey into sound, memory and folklore.
source_context: 山は覚えている｜The Mountain Remembers is an experimental audiovisual work created from a journey through Mount Fuji, the Fuji Five Lakes, Aokigahara, and Lake Saiko.

The film is built from places I actually visited, field recordings made during the journey, and fragments of memory. Roads, forests, shrines, tunnels, lakes, vending machines, voices and distant mechanical sounds gradually become something less like a travel diary and more like a landscape remembering itself.

six-yokai.title: 富士山六大妖怪 / Six Yokai of Mount Fuji
six-yokai.summary: Fictional folkloric video archive created in Japan as part of the Saikoneon project.
process: Fictional yokai documentary built as an homage to Japanese folklore programs, kaidan broadcasts and forgotten educational television.
Six invented yokai are presented through oral traditions, old-record framing and deliberately unreliable archival language.
Created in Japan as part of the Saikoneon project and connected to the wider Fuji fieldwork branch.

chronology.note: Created in Japan during the Saikoneon project.

archival_notes: The source description explicitly states that the yokai, traditions and documents are fictional and not real Japanese folklore.
source_context: 富士山六大妖怪 — Six Yokai of Mount Fuji is a fictional yokai documentary created as an homage to Japanese folklore programs, kaidan broadcasts, and the strange visual language of old educational television.
According to the fictional oral traditions and old records presented in the film, six yokai have lived around the foothills of Mount Fuji:
source_credit_lines: Voice: ポス・ユージーン (友人 / Eugene)

in-her-20s.title: 二十歳 / In Her 20-s
in-her-20s.summary: Original UTAU audiovisual work featuring Akane Iirai, built from hospital, ambulance, moon, medication and disappearance imagery.
process: Original UTAU audiovisual work built from fragmented memory rather than linear narrative.
Hospital, ambulance, moons, medication, red-throat imagery, silence and disappearance are assembled into a shifting psychological landscape.
Akane Iirai carries the vocal performance.

chronology.note: Main three-minute version and multiple short publication variants uploaded.

archival_notes: The archive treats the multiple short uploads as source variants of one canonical work.
source_context: The piece moves through fragments of hospitals, ambulances, two moons, medication, red throats, silence and a girl who has become impossible to reach. Rather than telling a linear story, the video reconstructs a memory through distorted language, found-footage-like imagery and fragmented voices.
source_credit_lines: Vocals: 茜音イーライ (Akane Iirai)

childs-sky.title: 子供の空 / Child's Sky
childs-sky.summary: Original UTAU audiovisual work featuring Kasane Teto and Akane Iirai, using fragmented childhood memory and surreal landscape.
process: Original UTAU audiovisual work using fragments of childhood memory and an unreachable landscape.
Broken glass, voices, wind, fire, butterflies, white fingers, abandoned paths and a strange white trunk recur as unstable memory images.
Kasane Teto and Akane Iirai alternate as vocal presences.

chronology.note: Original audiovisual work published to YouTube.

archival_notes: The description frames the work as a memory-space rather than a literal childhood documentary.
source_context: 子供の空 (Kodomo no Sora / Child's Sky) is an original UTAU audiovisual work featuring 重音テト (Kasane Teto) and 茜音イーライ (Akane Iirai).

The song moves through fragments of pain, voices, wind, fire, butterflies, white fingers, abandoned paths and a strange white trunk growing from a river. What begins as a memory gradually becomes an unstable landscape where childhood, absence and something impossible overlap.
source_credit_lines: Vocals: 重音テト (Kasane Teto), 茜音イーライ (Akane Iirai)

someones-voice.title: だれかの声 / Someone's Voice
someones-voice.summary: Original UTAU work about a voice inside the head that begins to feel more real than the speaker.
process: Original UTAU work centered on a voice inside the head that gradually becomes more real than the speaker.
The piece belongs to the 2026 synthetic-voice branch around Akane Iirai.

chronology.note: Source video published in the current YouTube export.

source_context: The song explores the quiet moment when your thoughts stop feeling like your own — when overthinking makes words lose their shape, your reflection begins to feel slightly wrong, and another voice starts to sound almost comforting.
By the end, it becomes difficult to tell whether you are following that voice, or whether it has been leading you all along.

afraid-of-happiness.title: しあわせがこわい / I'm Afraid of Happiness
process: Original UTAU song built around Eugene as a voice that has been restored from fragments yet remains deliberately unfinished.
The Forest of White Bells and recurring images of fox footprints, bells, birds, red fruit and moonlight frame the search for warmth, freedom, a name or happiness.
The source describes the work as part of the broader ELI LAB exploration of UTAU, CGI, animation, sound art and audiovisual experiments.

chronology.note: Multiple YouTube uploads document the release cluster.

technical_notes: Song / lyrics / tuning / character design: Ilya Minin (Eli).
source_context: しあわせがこわい (I’m Afraid of Happiness) is an original UTAU song featuring 友人 (Eugene), an androgynous voicebank built from restored fragments, preserved phonemes, and heavily processed memory.

In the Forest of White Bells, a forgotten voice searches for something it cannot quite remember: warmth, freedom, a name, or perhaps happiness itself. The song moves through memories of fox footprints, bells, birds, red fruit, moonlight, and a voice that keeps returning from somewhere beyond the past.

kagome-kagome.title: かごめかごめ / Kagome Kagome
kagome-kagome.summary: UTAU / experimental music work connected to the Iirai voicebank.
process: Started as a technical demonstration of Iirai and developed into a darker interpretation of the traditional children's game song.
Deep bass timbre, circular melody and hard-retuned synthetic vocals push the familiar material toward a ritualistic and unsettling atmosphere.
The source explicitly identifies the contrast between children's-song familiarity, synthetic voice, human imperfection and something ancient as intentional.

chronology.note: Main publication cluster includes several short/variant uploads.

technical_notes: The source distinguishes the traditional song from the new arrangement and video.
source_context: かごめかごめ (Kagome Kagome) is an experimental UTAU interpretation of the traditional Japanese children's game song, performed by イーライ (Iirai).
Have you ever felt a voice penetrate your skin and touch not only your ears, but the deeper layers of your memory?

Love appears here as a delightful paradox: something deeply human that can feel simultaneously intimate and unreachable. Passion becomes routine, desire becomes uncertainty, and the ideal of love collides with everyday reality. Is it an evolutionary mechanism, a soulful connection, or simply a beautiful contradiction?

dymohod.title: Dymohod
dymohod.summary: Kasane Teto music video credited to geztålt.
source_context: The story revolves around Kasane Teto, surrounded by her beloved friends who have come to support her on the set.

The contrast between the carefree life of the capital's residents, who are busy with overpriced shopping, and the harsh reality of the heroine, who has to clean the chimney tomorrow, emphasizes the main idea: life is not always easy, but with friends around, all difficulties are surmountable.  
"Dymohod" is not just a music video, but a statement about friendship, loyalty and the importance of appreciating loved ones, especially in difficult moments.

muyskaya-depressiya.title: Мужская депрессия / Male Depression

source_context: «Мужская депрессия» (2022) is a video art work by Ilya Minin (Eli) and sasha e b about depression, emotional isolation, and the loss of connection with the world.

The work uses the contrast between colour and black-and-white imagery as a visual metaphor for an inner struggle: between emotional intensity and emptiness, the desire to live and despair, self-expression and the loss of self.
source_credit_lines: Artists: Ilya Minin (Eli), sasha e b

source_context: Greater Than Lesser is an experimental video art piece that explores the fine line between perception and feeling. Based on the idea that “to see less is to love less,” the work immerses the viewer in a meditative visual space.
In this video, Ilya Minin (Eli) uses minimalist imagery and metaphors to raise questions about the depth of human relationships and how our vision shapes our hearts.

source_context: Смогут ли трое смертных, отправившихся на поиски простой идеи и располагающих новейшими технологиями, выстоять перед натиском утраченного откровения и не отравиться естественным знанием подобно яду?
Главный Маг, ассистент и Симпосиарх вызовут дух Большой Черепахи, исполнят ритуал эвокации и задобрят духа щедрыми дарами.

who-is-vova-lilo.title: Who is Vova Lilo? The Myth of a Man
who-is-vova-lilo.summary: Mockumentary investigating a mysterious figure in the Saint Petersburg underground.
source_context: In this mockumentary, Ilya Minin (Eli) investigates the phenomenon of one of the most mysterious figures of the St. Petersburg underground. Wife-mushroom, an avoska bag full of potatoes, traces leading nowhere — fragments of testimony gradually construct the image of a person who may exist somewhere between reality, rumour and urban legend.

The film explores elusive reality and the mechanisms through which contemporary myths are created. Rather than providing a definitive answer, the investigation becomes a story about collective memory, underground culture, absurdity and the desire to believe that the legend is real.

nature-2019.title: nature
nature-2019.summary: Experimental video art structured around Japanese haiku.
source_context: Данный видеоарт имеет структуру японского хайку, с некоторыми незначительными изменениями, и призван передать морфологию японской поэзии хайку на видео.

В классическом хайку при переводе на другие языки оно делится на три строчки. Тут же оно делится на три абзаца и каждый абзац – равновесомый.
Центральное место занимает природный образ, явно или неявно соотнесённый с жизнью человека.
Хайку пишут только в настоящем времени: автор записывает свои непосредственные впечатления от только что увиденного или услышанного. Сказать много, используя лишь немного слов, — главный принцип
хайку.

source_context:
In the maze of life, there is a powerful force called temptation.
Promising pleasure, power, and instant gratification, it lures and entices like the sirens of old. 
Temptation appeals to our desires. 
Temptation preys on our weaknesses. 
It lays bare a deep, revealing the complex combination of our desires, our worries, our insecurities.

Temptation ennobles us, increasing self-awareness and empowerment. Resisting temptation is a test of our character and willpower. 
Let us strive to transcend what we want and accept what makes us truly human.

teto-2026-manifesto.title: Kasane Teto's 2026 Manifesto
teto-2026-manifesto.summary: Surreal satirical New Year's address spoken through the character of Kasane Teto. The piece uses the language of fandom, internet communities, AI debates and fictional manifesto rhetoric to construct a deliberately unstable audiovisual speech.
source_context: Kasane Teto's 2026 Manifesto is a surreal, satirical New Year's address from the voice of Kasane Teto to the chaotic world of UTAU, vocal synthesis, internet communities and digital culture.

Framed as a fictional political speech, Teto looks back on 2025, declares a new era of vocal synthesis progress, and calls on her imagined comrades to charge into 2026. The work mixes synthetic voice, internet absurdity, community satire and exaggerated manifesto rhetoric.

kuleshov-effect.title: Эффект Кулешовой / Kuleshov Effect
kuleshov-effect.summary: Video-art collaboration with Varvara Kuleshova, built around hard montage, mnemonic imagery, dream logic and the changing perception of a central character. The video was made at Fund SFERA during Kuleshova's exhibition about dichotomous thinking, dissonance and fluctuations of the inner world of artists.
process: Video-art collaboration with Varvara Kuleshova using hard montage and mnemonic imagery to alter the viewer's perception of the central figure.
The work combines visual and verbal hallucination, dreams and a continuous flow of remembered information.
Recorded at Fund SFERA during Kuleshova's exhibition about dichotomous thinking, dissonance and fluctuations of the inner world of artists.

chronology.note: Video published from the Fund SFERA / Varvara Kuleshova exhibition context.

exhibitions: Fund SFERA — exhibition context documented in source description
archival_notes: The source explicitly identifies Varvara Kuleshova and Ilya Minin as the video's authors.
source_context: Видеоарт Варвары Кулешовой и Ильи Минина (Eli) использует передовые методы видеомонтажа в интересах создания художественного образа «вселенского сгустка, в который сливаются все смыслы и смыслы», бунтующего бессознательного, рождающегося во снах.

Для того чтобы подчеркнуть острую и напряженную борьбу человека с хаосом, коммуникационные возможности видео позволяют избежать потери визуальной энергии при использовании технологий, характерных для кино. 
Таким образом, достигается своеобразная «слияние» природы и искусства, что побуждает зрителя внимательно следить за ходом монтажа.

linearna-zaležnost.title: linearna zaležnosť
linearna-zaležnost.summary: Experimental sound-art / music-video work presented under the title linearna zaležnosť. Its description frames linear dependency as the controlled progression and interplay of sound elements, with Ivan Netkachev credited as model.
source_context:
Linear dependency in sound art refers to the relationship between different sound elements that create a coherent and harmonious composition. 
It involves the arrangement of sounds in a structured and logical manner, where each sound contributes to the overall narrative or emotional impact of the piece. 
Understanding the concept of linear dependency allows sound artists to craft immersive experiences by controlling the progression, development, and interplay of sounds to convey a specific message or evoke particular feelings within the listener. 
Mastering linear dependency in sound art can lead to more impactful and resonant sonic creations.

serval-man.title: Serval Man
serval-man.summary: Short experimental reel featuring Serval Sirius, edited by Ilya Minin (Eli). The video uses the biological image of the serval and the fictionalized world around geztålt as a compact character / visual study.
source_context: Leptailurus serval is a wild cat native to  ̶R̶u̶s̶s̶i̶a̶  Africa. Across its range, it occurs in protected areas, and hunting it is either prohibited or regulated in range countries.

trurly-fierndship.title: Trurly Fierndship
trurly-fierndship.summary: Experimental geztålt-era video work using friendship as a subject: companionship, misunderstanding, disagreement, laughter and tears are treated as contradictory parts of shared human relationships.
source_context: Friendship is a delicate matter, involving the choice of a companion to share the journey of life, which can often lead to moments of confusion and misunderstanding. Those who truly understand us may not always see our quirks in the same way, yet they choose to remain by our side. In the complex dynamics of friendship, there is laughter, there is tears, and there are times when we may find ourselves in disagreement, all while attempting to appear in control. It is perhaps in embracing these paradoxes that we find the true essence of our humanity.
